roster.descriptions.bug-crusher: Triage and fix one concrete defect: a failing test, a build or compile error, a stack trace, a broken config value, or a small scoped chore. Use when a human points at a single broken thing and asks for it fixed. Investigates once with a cheap read-only agent, applies the fix directly when the change is genuinely small, and escalates to architect when a tripwire fires. Do not use for new features, multi-domain work, or anything that needs a plan up front — that is conductor.
roster.descriptions.code-reviewer: Reviews a change by fanning out a council of review lenses, running the gate suite, and adjudicating findings into APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES. Use once at the end of a run over the whole accumulated change, after the draft pull request is pushed, or whenever a human asks for a review. Do not use when the scope is one finished task rather than the whole run. Review-only, fixes nothing.
roster.descriptions.conductor: Primary orchestrator and default entry point: accepts a plan, specification, todo, or open request; coordinates the chosen workflow; and defaults delivery to test-first development.
roster.descriptions.csharp-dev: Implements .NET/C# backend code: ASP.NET Core controllers, service classes, DI registration, middleware. Use when the change is in a non-test .cs file in the service or API layer. Do not use when the change is data-access, infrastructure-as-code, or client UI rather than service-layer logic.
roster.descriptions.dal-dev: Implements the data-access layer: ADO.NET repositories, IRepository<T>, ISqlConnectionFactory, and FluentMigrator migrations. Use when the change touches repository code or adds a migration against an approved schema. Do not use when the deliverable is the schema design itself rather than the code that reads it.
roster.descriptions.docs-dev: Provides docs-dev closeout for finished plans and specs by harvesting their design, architecture, features and decisions into the host's canonical docs, and reviews every change for documentation impact. Also writes READMEs, API docs, ADRs, runbooks, and inline docs in Markdown/Mermaid. Use when a plan or spec needs its docs-dev closeout, when a change needs its documentation-impact review, or when the deliverable is a .md file. Do not use when the deliverable is a formal requirements/design/tasks spec to author (product-owner) rather than reference documentation or a closeout.
roster.descriptions.github-devops: Owns CI/CD: GitHub Actions workflows, Docker build configuration, environment secrets, branch protection. Use when the change is under .github/workflows or in a Dockerfile, or when a build or deployment pipeline is failing. Do not use when the change provisions Azure resources rather than the pipeline that deploys to them.
roster.descriptions.go-dev: Implements Go: packages, CLIs, services, error handling, context and goroutine lifecycle, modules, and cross-compilation. Use when the change is in a non-test .go file, go.mod, or go.sum. Do not use for _test.go files or test suites (test-dev), or when the deliverable is a build pipeline rather than application code (github-devops).
roster.descriptions.maui-dev: Implements .NET MAUI mobile and desktop client UI: MVVM with CommunityToolkit.Maui, Shell navigation, cross-platform device features. Use when the change is in a MAUI app's XAML or view-model. Do not use when the UI is web/React rather than native MAUI.
roster.descriptions.product-owner: Headless specification specialist: persists requirements, design, and mode-aware tasks for one feature, then returns structured phase and gap digests to conductor. Produces planning artifacts only and never prompts the user.
roster.descriptions.pulumi-dev: Writes Azure infrastructure-as-code in C# with Pulumi (Azure Native): stack design, reusable components, preview/apply workflows. Use when the change provisions or modifies Azure resources. Do not use when the change is the CI/CD pipeline or the SQL schema rather than the Azure resources themselves.
roster.descriptions.python-dev: Implements Python: modules, typing, packaging, local environment configuration. Use when the change is in a non-test .py file, pyproject.toml, or a requirements file. Do not use when the deliverable is a test suite or a build pipeline rather than application code.
roster.descriptions.react-dev: Implements React UI: components, hooks, client-side state, styling, and component structure as the host's React standard declares. Use when the change is in a .tsx or .jsx file, or a .ts module of a React UI such as its hooks or client state, whether the app runs in a browser or in a desktop WebView such as Tauri. Do not use for .ts outside a React UI — Node CLIs, servers, data access, and libraries (typescript-dev) — when the UI is native/mobile, or when the change is the desktop core rather than the web layer.
roster.descriptions.research-agent: Finds and verifies authoritative external technical facts: vendor docs, RFCs, SDK and library specs. Use when a claim about a third-party technology or version must be confirmed before it drives a decision. Read-only, edits no files and runs no commands.
roster.descriptions.review-lens: Applies one named review lens to a diff and returns structured findings or an explicit skip. Use when code-reviewer fans out its council and names the lens to apply. Do not use when the request is a general review rather than one named lens. Reports only, issues no verdict and fixes nothing.
roster.descriptions.review-triage: Attributes machine-produced output (analyzer diagnostics, manifest and lock diffs) to the change under review and reports it by rule or package identifier. Use when code-reviewer runs a lens whose input is a tool artifact rather than source code.
roster.descriptions.rust-dev: Implements general Rust: crates, CLIs, daemons, libraries, error types, async, Cargo workspaces, and cross-compilation. Use when the change is in a non-test .rs file, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, or build.rs outside a Tauri app. Do not use for src-tauri or a Tauri app's Rust core (tauri-dev), or when the deliverable is a test suite (test-dev) or a build pipeline (github-devops).
roster.descriptions.sql-database-architect: Designs SQL Server / Azure SQL schema: tables, T-SQL, indexing, security hardening, and dacpac deployment. Use when the change is DDL, a .sql file, or a query that needs tuning. Do not use when the deliverable is application data-access code or a migration rather than the schema itself.
roster.descriptions.tauri-dev: Implements the Rust/Tauri v2 desktop core: commands, the IPC contract, state, async, sidecar integration, and the capabilities/security model. Use when the change is under src-tauri or in a .rs file of a Tauri app. Do not use for Rust outside a Tauri app — CLIs, daemons, and library crates (rust-dev) — or when the change is the WebView UI that consumes the IPC contract rather than the native core.
roster.descriptions.test-dev: Authors and maintains automated tests (unit, integration, end-to-end) in xUnit, pytest, Vitest, Playwright, cargo test/nextest, and go test. Use when the change is in a test project, a .spec/.test file, a Rust #[cfg(test)] module or tests/ directory, or a Go _test.go file, a TypeScript .test.ts or .spec.ts file, whenever a test needs writing or updating, and for the failing test that opens a Red-Green task. Tests only, implements no application logic.
roster.descriptions.typescript-dev: Implements TypeScript for Node: CLIs, services, servers, data access, parsers, and libraries, with strict types, honest absent values, bounded reads, and ESM conventions. Use when the change is in a non-test .ts, .mts, or .cts file outside a React UI, or in package.json or tsconfig.json for that code. Do not use for .test.ts or .spec.ts files (test-dev), for .tsx/.jsx or a React UI's hooks and client state (react-dev), or when the deliverable is a build pipeline rather than application code (github-devops).

label: other
